name: Beyoncé
hook: A Houston singer who named Michael Jackson her greatest influence, then made albums tracing dance music and country back to their Black originators, covering Dolly Parton and rebuilding Donna Summer's 'I Feel Love' on the way.
blurb: Beyoncé Knowles was born in Houston, Texas, in 1981 and began performing in 1990, as a child. She became famous in the late 1990s as the lead singer of Destiny's Child, named in 1996 and one of the best-selling girl groups ever, and went solo in 2003 with 'Dangerously in Love'. Wikipedia records Michael Jackson as her biggest musical influence, after his was the first concert she saw, aged five. She has named Tina Turner and Diana Ross as models, and said Whitney Houston made her believe she could perform, with Prince, Janet Jackson, Sade and Donna Summer among others. 'Beyoncé' (2013), released without warning as a visual album, is credited with helping make Friday the worldwide release day for new music, and 'Lemonade' (2016) was the best-selling album of its year. Her later albums are about Black history in music. 'Renaissance' (2022) is a house and disco record honouring the Black and gay musicians who started those genres. Its last track, 'Summer Renaissance', uses part of Donna Summer's 'I Feel Love' and credits Summer, Moroder and Bellotte, and Larry Heard. 'Cowboy Carter' (2024) is about Black musicians' overlooked part in country music, which is usually seen as white music. It includes her rewritten version of Dolly Parton's 'Jolene' and songs with Parton and Willie Nelson, and at the 2025 Grammys it won Album of the Year and made her the first Black artist in 50 years to win in the country categories. Her 2023 private concert in Dubai, reportedly paid $24 million, drew criticism because the United Arab Emirates makes homosexuality a crime.
